item.ptxt: While the vehicle is being driven after the engine has warmed up, the engine control computer performs active air-fuel ratio control for approximately 30 seconds or more. At this time, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition. During this time, deterioration of the three-way catalyst and malfunctions of the oxygen sensor are detected.

During active air-fuel ratio control, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition. If the oxygen sensor malfunctions, the amount of change in its output voltage becomes small.

If the oxygen sensor outputs voltage only between 0.21 V and 0.59 V during active air-fuel ratio control, the engine control computer judges that the oxygen sensor voltage is abnormal and stores P0136/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.
Open or short in oxygen sensor circuit
During active air-fuel ratio control, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition.

If the oxygen sensor output voltage is 0.21 V or less (lean) even though the active air-fuel ratio control target is rich, the engine control computer judges that there is a malfunction in the oxygen sensor circuit and stores P0137/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.

If the oxygen sensor output voltage is 0.59 V or more (rich) even though the active air-fuel ratio control target is lean, the engine control computer judges that there is a malfunction in the oxygen sensor circuit and stores P0138/27. It then illuminates the check engine warning light.
When all of the following conditions are met
Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher
Throttle valve is not fully closed
Engine speed is less than 4000 r/min
Air-fuel ratio feedback control in progress
Fuel cut is not being performed
Same as P0136/27 (oxygen sensor voltage malfunction)
Same as P0136/27 (oxygen sensor voltage malfunction)
When either of the following conditions is met
When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.3 or less (rich target), the oxygen sensor output voltage stays only between 0.21 V and 0.59 V.
When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.9 or more (lean target), the oxygen sensor output voltage stays only between 0.21 V and 0.59 V.
When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.3 or less (rich target), the oxygen sensor output voltage is less than 0.21 V
When the air-fuel ratio control target value is 14.9 or more (lean target), the oxygen sensor output voltage is 0.59 V or more

topic.title: Confirmation Driving
topic.ptxt: By performing confirmation driving, it is possible to check whether the DTC is reproduced.

item.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) display screen, clear the DTCs. (see ) (A)
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes. (Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher) (B)
Drive the vehicle at 60 to 100 km/h for 10 minutes or more. (C)
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, check the DTC judgment result. (see )

atten2.ptxt: When performing this driving test, be sure to obey speed limits and other traffic laws.

atten4.ptxt: If the DTC judgment result is "judging" or "cannot judge", drive the vehicle again at 60 to 100 km/h for 10 minutes or more (D), then check the DTC judgment result. If the result is still "judging" or "cannot judge", drive the vehicle again at 75 to 100 km/h for 10 minutes or more (E), then check the DTC judgment result.
The malfunctioning area can be identified by performing the [Injection Volume] active test. This active test can decrease the fuel injection volume by -12.5% or increase it by +24.8%.

item.ptxt: Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON.
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes. (Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher)
Maintain the engine speed at 2500 r/min for approximately 3 minutes to warm up each sensor.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select [Active Test] - [Fuel Injection Volume], and select [ECU Data Monitor] - [A/F Sensor Voltage B1S1] and [O2 Sensor Voltage B1S2].

With the engine idling, read the output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor when the fuel injection volume is increased and decreased using the Active Test [Fuel Injection Volume].

specitem.ptxt: The output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor change according to the increase and decrease in fuel injection volume.
